graphEvents.label: Documented truthy disable grammar lives in a second module
Documented SPECKIT_SPEC_GATE_DISABLED alias has no reader in the named file
The only deny is destructible by its own telemetry write
Warning log cannot distinguish deny from advise
ENV-REFERENCE drift guard covers 118 of 251 documented names

label: ENV-REFERENCE documents SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_DISABLED as a truthy disable flag (1/true/yes/on) but spec-gate-core.mjs compares against the exact string '1' at five read sites; the wider grammar is honoured only by isHookEnabled in .skilled/hooks/shared/hook-flags.cjs, reached through a six-level createRequire whose catch returns false, so one documented variable has two readers with two grammars and an install without the hooks hub keeps only '1'.

The documented alias SPECKIT_SPEC_GATE_DISABLED has no reader in the file ENV-REFERENCE names as its reader (hooks/lib/spec-gate/spec-gate-core.mjs) and is not bridged by env-aliases.cjs, which rewrites only MK_ keys; its sole reader is the legacy-alias list in .skilled/hooks/shared/hook-flags.cjs, outside the documenting package. The same document also names the spec-gate plugin as both .opencode/plugins/system-spec-gate.js and plugins/system-spec-gate.js; only the former exists.

runEnforceGate resolves the gate state directory a second time for its warning-log write, outside any try and without the projectDir||process.cwd() fallback that evaluateMutation applies, so a throw there discards an already-computed deny and the adapter's terminal catch converts the whole call into approve(); the gate's only blocking path is destructible by its own telemetry write. Repro: four stdin payloads (valid with unreadable cwd, invalid JSON, empty, Bash) all produce exit 0 with empty stdout and stderr.

spec-gate-warnings.log derives its decision field from result.wouldDeny rather than from the decision returned, and wouldDeny is denyCapable (true for every Write/Edit) regardless of enforcement, so an advisory and an enforced denial are both logged as would-deny; the gate's only durable record cannot show whether it has ever blocked a mutation.

The ENV-REFERENCE drift guard enforces documentation in one direction only, for one prefix, over one dialect: ENV_READ_RE requires the SPECKIT_ prefix, collectRuntimeTsFiles skips every non-.ts file so all runtime/hooks/**/*.mjs readers are out of scope, and the broader extension scan is limited to runtime/cli. Measured against the document's own table: 133 of 251 documented names are non-SPECKIT_ and structurally unreachable by the assertion, and 191 have no reader text inside runtime/ at all. The document's claim that every name has a verified reader is unenforced in the doc-to-code direction.

specGateConcernDisabled returns false from its catch, so a load failure of the hooks hub is indistinguishable from an unset switch and the operator's kill switch silently re-arms the gate; every other defensive branch in the file fails in the permissive direction. Concrete extension: return a tri-state and append one warning-log line naming the module that failed to resolve on the unknown branch.
